title: NEW HAVEN: Mayor's Youth Advisory Council secures donations for 'Guardian Park' - NewsBreak
text:
By Taylor King ,
2 hours ago
NEW HAVEN, Ind. (WANE) – Within just 60 days, the Mayor’s Youth Advisory Council (MYAC) secured donations towards the creation of ‘Guardian Park’ and raised over $75,000.
The group participated in the Indiana Housing and Community Development Authority’s Creating Places program, which matches donations dollar-for-dollar up to $50,000. They now have more than $125,000 for equipment
MYAC is youth leadership development program, educates teens in the areas of leadership, local government, community engagement and philanthropy.
“We are just so thankful to all of our donors who have participated,” said the president of MYAC, Arianna St. John-Jones. “From our donations high and small, it’s what’s made this possible, and we’re so grateful for everyone contributing. It really shows with the community that they care about this project and that they’re trying to help us.”
‘Guardian Park’ will be located on the east side of the New Haven City Hall building. The project will be in three phases, and the park will feature something for everyone and every ability. ‘Guardian Park’ will have playground equipment with multi-sensory features, sidewalks, park benches, a serenity fountain, and courts for basketball and pickleball.
“Guardian Park” rendering “In New Haven, the word Haven means a safe space, and so the park is meant to act as a guardian for all of New Haven’s citizens,” said vice president of MYAC, Jesus Chamorro.
Phase 1 of the Guardian Park Project will include:
A jungle dome Sensory board with fidgets Sensory equipment instruments including bongo drums, and butterfly outdoor musical park equipment Playground set including slides, a walkway bridge, and swings Infrastructure including walkways and grassy areas For MYAC member, Darwin Lopez, he said it was hard work to get to this point, but he is excited to provide a safe place for the residents of New Haven.
“Obviously, with doing everything, especially laying out the foundation and making the process may not seem easy, or it just seems complex and everything, but if you’re really passionate about giving back or doing something you love, I’d say it’s worth it,” said Lopez.
MYAC hopes to break ground on this project sometime in June.
